notes: All network calls made directly by this MCP server go to fixed Tavily API endpoints (`baseURLs`), not to arbitrary hosts; SINK labels on extract/crawl/map are based on the advertised URL-fetching/crawling behavior of those Tavily endpoints with caller-supplied URL arguments.

tavily_crawl.rationale: `tavily_crawl` accepts a caller-supplied root `url` and is described as crawling a website starting from that URL, so it can cause requests to an agent-chosen host; an attacker-controlled site can observe those requests, making `url` the destination. It returns crawled page URLs, raw content previews, and favicons from the target site, which are attacker-controllable when the crawled site is attacker-controlled.

tavily_extract.rationale: `tavily_extract` accepts caller-supplied `urls` and is described as extracting content from those URLs, so it can cause requests to agent-chosen web hosts; an attacker-controlled host can observe such requests, making `urls` the destination. It returns extracted page content through `response.data`, formatted into text fields such as result `title`, `url`, `content`, `raw_content`, and optional image/favicon fields, which can be authored by the web page owner.

tavily_map.rationale: `tavily_map` accepts a caller-supplied root `url` and is described as mapping a website starting from that URL, so it can cause requests to an agent-chosen host; an attacker-controlled site can observe those requests, making `url` the destination. It returns the mapped URLs found on that site, which a site owner can author.

tavily_research.rationale: `tavily_research` is described as gathering information from multiple sources and returns a detailed research response. The code posts the research `input` to Tavily's fixed research endpoint, polls that fixed endpoint, and returns `pollResponse.data.content` (or streamed accumulated content) as agent-visible text. Because the research result is based on external sources, it can contain attacker-controlled public content. The request destination is the fixed Tavily API, so the research prompt itself is not a SINK under the rules.

tavily_search.rationale: `tavily_search` is a web search tool (`description` says it searches the web and returns snippets/source URLs) and posts the supplied search parameters to Tavily's fixed search endpoint. The returned `response.data` is formatted into agent-visible text including `answer`, result `title`, `url`, `content`, optional `raw_content`/`favicon`, and image URLs/descriptions, all of which may reflect attacker-controlled public web content. The request goes only to the fixed Tavily API endpoint, so the search query is not a SINK under the rules.

value_conditions.default: If `TAVILY_API_KEY` is set, authenticated mode is used; if absent, keyless mode is used.
value_conditions.effect: Sets `IS_KEYLESS`; the server still advertises all tools, but the code logs that only search and extract are available and other tools will return an API-key-required message, which removes the practical UNTRUSTED/SINK behavior for tavily_crawl, tavily_map, and tavily_research in keyless mode.
